policy.support: The cited evidence set, read together and without outside knowledge, entails the entire claim.

evidence: SPIRIT-AI and CONSORT-AI Working Group Reporting guidelines for clinical trial reports for interventions involving artificial intelligence: the CONSORT-AI Extension.

Investigators seeking to report studies developing and validating the diagnostic and predictive properties of AI models should refer to TRIPOD-ML and STARD-AI, both of which are currently under development.
cases.claim: SPIRIT-AI works with TRIPOD-ML before full clinical trials.

evidence: DECIDE-AI is focused on the evaluation stage and does not prescribe a fixed study design.
cases.claim: DECIDE-AI focuses on the evaluation stage without prescribing a fixed study design.

evidence: Protocol alpha reduced review errors by 37 percent.
cases.claim: Review errors fell by 37% under protocol alpha.

evidence: The intervention did not increase the rate of serious adverse events.
cases.claim: Serious adverse-event rates were not increased by the intervention.

evidence: The trial enrolled 240 adults.
Participants were randomly assigned in equal numbers to intervention and control groups.
cases.claim: The trial randomly assigned 120 adults to each group.

evidence: In cohort A, the intervention reduced review errors by 37 percent.
In cohort B, the intervention reduced review errors by 22 percent.
cases.claim: The intervention reduced review errors in both cohorts.

evidence: Labs were notable for creatinine (Cr) 1.7, compared with a baseline creatinine of 0.5.
cases.claim: The patient's creatinine was elevated above baseline.

evidence: CONSORT-AI is intended for reports of randomized clinical trials evaluating interventions with an artificial intelligence component.
cases.claim: CONSORT-AI applies to reports of randomized trials evaluating AI interventions.

evidence: Model A had sensitivity of 0.91, whereas Model B had sensitivity of 0.84 on the same test set.
cases.claim: Model A was more sensitive than Model B on that test set.

evidence: No material source disagreements were identified.
cases.claim: No material source disagreements were identified.

evidence: The prespecified primary endpoint was diagnostic accuracy at 30 days.
Diagnostic accuracy at 30 days was 88 percent in the external validation cohort.
cases.claim: The external validation cohort achieved 88% on the prespecified primary endpoint.

evidence: Protocol alpha reduced review errors by 37 percent.

evidence: SPIRIT-AI covers clinical trial protocols. CONSORT-AI covers clinical trial reports.
cases.claim: SPIRIT-AI was derived from CONSORT-AI.

evidence: Use of the tool was associated with lower review-error rates in an observational cohort.
cases.claim: The tool caused the reduction in review errors.

evidence: Model A had sensitivity of 0.91. Model B had specificity of 0.94.
cases.claim: Model A performed better overall than Model B.

evidence: Three of four evaluated hospitals reported improved workflow.

evidence: The primary analysis showed a statistically significant reduction.
